extension.summary: Particle Life tuned for 32-bit Android Kodi
extension.description:
The same Particle Life as "Particle Life (OpenGL)", built for 32-bit Android (armeabi-v7a), as on many Fire TV sticks, Google TV boxes and the Chromecast with Google TV. Install this one if your Android or Google TV Kodi is a 32-bit app; install "Particle Life (OpenGL)" on 64-bit Android and macOS. A few kinds of particles attract or repel each other according to a small square matrix of pair forces, and out of that come cells, worms, membranes, orbiting rings and drifting colonies. Ten presets reproduce the best matrices from the original Particle Life demo (DNA, Worm, Waves, Soap, Photon, Ladybug, Flower, Cells, Vacuum, Y); type any matrix of your own, or let it invent a completely random one and start again with new rules whenever it restarts.
The simulation is CPU-side and built for weak boxes: a uniform neighbour grid rebuilt each step by a counting sort makes a step cost the particles plus the pairs inside the radius rather than every possible pair, positions are interpolated between fixed steps so motion is smooth even when the simulation runs at 30 steps a second, and the scene is drawn into a capped offscreen target that fades itself for soft trails, then scaled up once. This build starts at 2,048 particles, a 10% radius and a 720p target; all of those can be raised or lowered from the settings, up to 32,768 particles and full-resolution output on a device that can afford it. Species, force, damping, start pattern, palette, colour style, size, glow, trails, background, dimming, restart and evolve intervals are all settable.
extension.disclaimer: This is a native add-on: it is built per platform and Kodi version (this one: Kodi 21 Omega, 32-bit ARM Android). It needs OpenGL ES 2.0. Particle Life was created by Hunar Ahmad (https://github.com/hunar4321/life_code, MIT); this is an independent native port of the same idea, with the interaction matrices taken from that project's "interesting models".
